reuse.why: Every midpoint copy (schedules app x2, forecast, template, preview) is routed to one new shared getExpectedAmount using the existing getApproxNumberThreshold, but the already-exported getScheduledAmount helper was not made the definition and instead re-dispatches around it.

duplication.why: Six inline copies are removed; the remaining overlap is getScheduledAmount repeating the null/number/range dispatch of getExpectedAmount instead of delegating to it.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts next to getScheduledAmount, used by server modules and the API model as the tree's layering expects.

scope.why: Changes are limited to the amount rule, its consumers, the API field and release notes.

maintainability.why: One rule function is easy to change, but two overlapping public helpers (getExpectedAmount and getScheduledAmount with an op parameter) leave ambiguity about which to call.

disguised_duplication.where: packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts getScheduledAmount: re-does the null/number/range dispatch, calling getExpectedAmount only for numbers and getRangedAmount for ranges, instead of delegating fully

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gained an op parameter for the approximate rule; getExpectedAmount gained the isapprox branch as part of the rule itself; all amount sites call the shared functions
